Subject: MS D1 Sales: Clients are weary
Sender: ruth.borland@morganstanley.com
Received: 2026-09-28T08:54:46

Sentiment across sales and trading desks as we head into quarter-end is not encouraging – most trading desks set up in “wait and see” mode, with a distinct lack of client re-engagement on the Q1 favourite global thematics. The turmoil in Rates markets last week only reinforced the perceived lack of control in fiscal and monetary policy, with the long end of the Treasury curve pushed to generational extremes (30Y at 5.51%, highest since 2004), leaving US 30y fixed mortgages at 7.18% today. Add to this a challenging performance through September (Global L/S HFs down ~1% MTD), further supporting the sentiment that the P&L for 2026 was made in Q1, with those who have it desperate to protect it – largely through lower Gross Exposure.

On the flipside, clients and trading desks are equally paranoid that a Trump pre-election headline around a resolution in Hormuz could trigger a major index rally and reversal in rates – the FOMO is palpable. The contradiction in these points results in an awkward asymmetry into Q4. Our conversations are therefore increasingly focused on using hedges to create room to run more risk – preserving downside protection while keeping enough exposure on the books to participate if Q4 gives investors something to chase.

According to our PB Content team, HFs ended net buyers of global equities via long additions last week, as the pace of re-grossing accelerated primarily across US equities post FOMC. Positioning wise, HF net exposure has continued to increase meaningfully across Agentic AI names (MSXXCLAW) and Hyperscalers, as the cohort has continued to lean into less-crowded pockets of the AI trade, while net positioning in Memory (MSXXGMEM) remains well off peak levels at ~6% of global net exposure (vs. ~12% at peaks). Despite the active re-grossing flow across US equities, US-based L/S fund gross leverage across their global portfolios has remained near lows vs the last 12m. European equities ended net sold over the week as HFs largely pressed shorts – though, the selling was led entirely by Industrials as HFs were sellers of EU Aerospace & Defense (MSESAER) and EU Industrial Transports (MSESITR).

We had a bumper week last week in new Equity Thematics launched last week, with some new tradable baskets to consider alongside this. We are getting considerable traction on our short EU AI Agent Risk basket (MSSTARSK) idea – as global investors don’t find it hard to imagine a scenario where the fragmented European Telecoms, Classifieds and Ticketing sectors get threatened by automation of product discovery, comparison, negotiation and purchasing decisions.

In the UK - the Government announced the "Your First Home": 2.5% deposits plus a 20% equity loan for FTBs buying new-builds. This should support eligible new-build demand: in the first five years of Help to Buy (2013–2018), combined completions across Persimmon, Taylor Wimpey and Barratt rose by roughly 33%. This morning our UK Homebuilders basket (MSSTUKHB) is up ~11.5%. Please ask if you would like to discuss positioning & flows here.

Mentioned last week, but worth re-flagging, there was also an excellent note from Chris Metli last week highlighting a significant drop off in retail activity. This September estimated average daily retail demand is down 23% from August, which was already the lightest month of the year.

Please let us know how we can help.

Kind regards,
Ruth Borland, Executive Director
